pt>en:c5abad9a30b32753: Thomas Goodwin, an English Puritan and one of the theologians of the Westminster Assembly, wrote a work with a long title and a simple question: after Jesus ascended to heaven and was glorified, does His heart remain the same with sinners? Or did glory make Him distant?
pt>en:7fe35c0c1970dd68: The ministry of the Spirit's spotlight
pt>en:c22d39d87422d1f8: A bold point from the book: Goodwin suggests that glory increased Christ's capacity to love, rather than diminishing it. He is freer and fuller to have compassion on His own. When a believer suffers or sins, Christ's heart moves toward him, to rescue and restore.
pt>en:6711b55d0a37fada: Goodwin answers firmly: the same. The Jesus who wept with Martha and Mary, who touched lepers and received sinners, is the Jesus who today is at the right hand of the Father. The ascension did not harden his heart. On the contrary, he remains human, with glorified human affections, and therefore sympathizes with our weaknesses (Hebrews 4:15).
pt>en:6b09f3ccd505e442: Keep in Step with the Spirit (1984)
pt>en:e0b4b1398b709dcf: Ligonier · articles about the Holy Spirit
pt>en:20249c50328aa352: For Packer, the greatest sign of the Spirit's presence is not the intensity of emotions nor the spectacular nature of the gifts, but holiness: the fruit of the Spirit described in Galatians 5, as love, joy, peace, patience, and self-control. He does not despise experiences; He only puts them in the right place. An experience that no longer produces love for Christ and more obedience must be examined.
pt>en:45f625b049efc284: Packer recalls what Jesus said about the Spirit: "He will glorify me" (John 16:14). A well-positioned spotlight illuminates a building at night, and no one looks at the lamp. That's how the Spirit is: it doesn't draw attention to itself, but points to Christ. Where Christ is exalted, known, and loved, there the Spirit is at work.
pt>en:9daf52c90b7954a4: The original title talks about keeping pace with the Spirit (Galatians 5:25). Packer describes the Christian life as a walk in which we follow the Spirit's guidance through the Word, prayer, and church fellowship. It is not passivity or activism, but humble cooperation: the Spirit works in us, and we work our salvation with fear and trembling (Philippians 2:12–13).
pt>en:86197d34df8faa1e: J. I. Packer wrote about the Holy Spirit at a time of much debate about gifts and experiences. Instead of entering only into controversy, he asked a deeper question: what is the central work of the Spirit? His answer became known by an image: the spotlight ministry.
pt>en:8d6f8b60fd1a8c20: The Spirit that unites us to Christ
pt>en:3d568109605e1f25: The Spirit in the life of Jesus
pt>en:868c816ca05055d8: Christ outside of us, Christ within us
pt>en:df571e432f72ea31: The doctrine of union with Christ brings deep comfort: everything that belongs to Christ is yours, and you belong to Him. In times of weakness, remember: you are not just trying to imitate Jesus from afar; His Spirit lives in you and binds you to Him forever.
pt>en:fdd9a9702e9bb848: Sinclair Ferguson, a Scottish theologian, wrote one of the most comprehensive and pastoral studies on the Holy Spirit in the Reformed tradition. A central theme runs through the book: the main work of the Spirit in salvation is to unite us to Christ.
pt>en:7dc18573ed5881b9: A beautiful contribution of the book is to show the Spirit working in Jesus' own life: in the conception, baptism, temptations in the desert, miracles, the cross, and resurrection. The same Spirit that led Jesus in all his work is given to the church. That is why the Christian life is a life shaped in the image of the Son.
pt>en:ce01ffc9ddf8e5d3: Packer leaves a useful criterion for evaluating movements, worship, and experiences: Is Christ being magnified? Do people leave loving Jesus, His Word, and His people more? If so, the spotlight is on in the right place.
pt>en:0254662f45c012a1: The work of the Holy Spirit
pt>en:dc2c411840d85259: Calvin said that while Christ remains outside of us, everything He suffered and did for our salvation is useless to us. Ferguson develops this idea: the Spirit is the bond that unites us to Christ. Through faith, which is the gift of the Spirit, we receive everything that is in Christ: justification, adoption, sanctification, and the hope of glory.
pt>en:52116c03bb1653c9: Ferguson insists that sanctification is not a moral effort apart from grace. United to Christ, we die with him to sin and rise with him to new life (Romans 6). The Spirit applies this reality day after day. We fight against sin not to achieve union with Christ, but because we are already united to him.
pt>en:ed595451c21434e6: The Work of the Holy Spirit (Het werk van den Heiligen Geest, 1888)
pt>en:3364849c6023f152: The Spirit in the church and in the individual
pt>en:24e7c74bdd73bca9: Then, Kuyper describes the work of the Spirit in salvation: he inspired the Scriptures, formed the body of Christ in Mary's womb, anointed Jesus in his ministry, regenerates sinners, produces faith, unites the believer to Christ, and sanctifies him. Everything Christ has gained, the Spirit applies.
pt>en:07b5aa82232687b1: Kuyper balances the communal and personal dimensions. The Spirit dwells in the church as a temple and also in every believer. He distributes gifts for the edification of all and produces fruits of love and holiness. A spirituality that despises the church or ignores the heart is incomplete.
pt>en:bc90de730a949760: Kuyper begins before salvation. The Spirit hovered over the waters in creation (Genesis 1:2). He gives life, order, and beauty to the world. Kuyper attributes to the Spirit even the natural gifts: the skill of the craftsman, the talent of the artist, the wisdom of the ruler. Bezalel, who built the tabernacle, was filled with the Spirit to work with art (Exodus 31). This means that no honest work is outside God's interest.
pt>en:6ce4b2a25856f071: The Work of the Holy Spirit (public domain) · search
pt>en:a3b000c7c4292938: Keller begins with the fact. The Christian faith does not rely on an abstract teaching, but on a historical event: the empty tomb and Jesus' appearances to many witnesses (1 Corinthians 15:3–8). He reminds us that if the resurrection did not happen, Christianity falls, as Paul himself admits. But if it did, everything changes.
pt>en:7c87d89c287b0fc2: Keller, in his last months of life, publicly said that illness had led him to believe in the resurrection in a more personal and real way than before. The book's invitation is the same: to let the resurrection cease to be just doctrine and become the hope that sustains today.
pt>en:b12f934b353f425c: The sky, a world of love
pt>en:280957526b3804c1: The resurrection of Jesus is the firstfruits of the harvest. It guarantees that those who are in it will also rise again. Keller insists that Christian hope is not to flee the world to a vacant heaven, but to wait for the renewal of all things: resurrected bodies, a new creation, full righteousness, and the presence of God among His people (Revelation 21).
pt>en:82a6aeab5da61901: Charity and Its Fruits, final sermon "Heaven Is a World of Love" (1738)
pt>en:4b74108ee80df257: Because of this, the Christian can face fear differently. Not denying pain, but knowing that death does not have the final word. Keller notes that the hope of resurrection has produced, throughout history, courageous Christians in caring for the sick, in the struggle for justice, and in faithfulness under persecution.
pt>en:484229c53c359450: Edwards starts from Paul's statement that love never ends (1 Corinthians 13:8). Faith will give way to vision, and hope to possession. But love remains and reaches perfection. That is why heaven can be described as the place where love is full: God's love poured out without limits and the love of the saints for one another, without envy, without pride, and without fear of losing.
pt>en:c77a6fac4b0aa638: The sermon ends with an appeal. If heaven is a world of love, whoever intends to get there must learn to love now. Edwards says that the Christian life is a journey toward that world, and that every act of true love is a taste of the homeland. Hell, by contrast, is a world without love. The question, then, is personal: is your heart being prepared for the place where only love dwells?
pt>en:742f58eaff6a4c1a: Edwards suggests something surprising: the joy of heaven will not be static. Since God is infinite, there will always be more to know and love. Eternity will not be boredom, but endless discovery.
pt>en:fc87e6a56c51ecee: Abraham Kuyper was a theologian, journalist, university founder, and prime minister of the Netherlands. Even with an intense political agenda, he wrote one of the most comprehensive treatises on the Holy Spirit in the Reformed tradition. Kuyper wanted to correct an oversight: many churches spoke of the Father and the Son, but almost nothing of the Spirit.
pt>en:392cd13ffa6b13b5: For Edwards, heaven is not beautiful because of golden streets, but because God is there, who is love. The Father, the Son, and the Spirit live in eternal communion, and the redeemed are brought into that love. Each one loves and is loved according to their ability, and all are satisfied, because no one desires what they do not have.
pt>en:0ee40f6757df4ff5: Tim Keller wrote Hope in Times of Fear during the pandemic while treating the cancer that would lead to his death in 2023. The theme is the resurrection of Jesus and what it means for those living in a world marked by fear and uncertainty. It is not a theoretical book: it is the hope of someone who looked at their own death.
pt>en:fd754c1ac42ad910: Kuyper's work broadens the perspective: the Spirit is present in worship and also in Monday work. Ask him not only for strength to pray, but for wisdom to work, creativity to serve, and love to live together. Every area of life is territory where the Spirit wants to act.
pt>en:75d0e21f5d91808d: Jonathan Edwards, pastor and theologian from New England, considered one of the greatest thinkers in American history, preached in 1738 a series of sermons on 1 Corinthians 13. The last of them has an unforgettable title: heaven is a world of love.
pt>en:cacde069617f746d: The Meaning of Marriage (2011), chapter on sexuality
pt>en:6e82d943902e09e4: John Bunyan was a poor tinsmith and Baptist preacher who spent twelve years imprisoned for preaching without a license. In prison, he wrote an allegory that became one of the most read books in history after the Bible: The Pilgrim. A Christian, the main character, leaves the City of Destruction and walks to the Heavenly City. The final scene is one of the most moving in Christian literature.
pt>en:8af5cf009465dde9: Sex as renewal of the alliance
pt>en:4cb6a9290e7a3bfe: The Pilgrim reminds us that we are strangers in this world, on the way to the homeland. It is worth asking: on what stretch of the path am I? And it is worth resting in the certainty of Hope: the riverbed is firm for those who are in Christ.
pt>en:83faedcecb72af1e: Grace for those who have already made mistakes
pt>en:bec8484d447ff280: On the other side, angels welcome the pilgrims, and they enter the city to the sound of trumpets. Bunyan describes the joy of those who arrive home. Death, for the believer, is not the end of the road, but the last crossing before glory.
pt>en:8fd24d3660730b9d: Upon approaching the Heavenly City, the pilgrim finds a deep river, without a bridge. It is the image of death. Christian is afraid and almost drowns, overwhelmed by memories of his sins. His companion, Hopeful, holds him and says he feels the depths, and that the depths are good. Then Christians remember Christ and the promise of Isaiah 43:2: when you pass through the waters, I will be with you. And cross over.
pt>en:ae7c0c69e0da19a9: Keller responds to common objections: "but we love each other" or "we need to know if we match." He argues that sex before commitment tends to create false intimacy, without the security of promise, and ends up teaching the person to protect themselves rather than surrender. Waiting is not repression; it is preparation for a complete surrender.
pt>en:df198649b4f16935: Keller's most well-known image is that sex is an act of renewing the covenant. In marriage, husband and wife made a public promise to belong to each other for life. In sexual relations, they say with the body what they promised with their mouth: "I am all yours, forever." Outside of marriage, the body says something that life is not saying. That is why the Bible reserves sex for marriage between a man and a woman.
pt>en:46498ec37980edc2: Before the end, the pilgrim passes through the Swamp of Discouragement, the Hill of Difficulty, the Valley of Humiliation, the Vanity Fair, and the Castle of Doubt. Bunyan portrays Christian life with realism: there are falls, temptations, and discouragements, but there are also faithful companions, shelter, and the cross, where the burden of guilt falls from the Christian's shoulders.
pt>en:b595f8549fafd05a: Keller begins by stating that the Bible is not against sex. It celebrates it, as seen in Song of Songs. Sex is good because it was created by God. But precisely because it is so powerful, it was given with a purpose: to unite two people entirely, body and soul, within a covenant.
pt>en:0ad7863de41d0bbe: In the book The Meaning of Marriage, Tim Keller dedicates an entire chapter to sex. He notes that the modern world treats sex as an appetite to be satisfied or as a form of personal expression, and that the Christian view is at once higher and more demanding.
pt>en:4c2a5cb1bd6bbc24: Keller also speaks to those who have lived differently. The gospel is not a court with no way out. In Christ there is complete forgiveness and a real new beginning. Purity is not just an untouched past, but a path that can be chosen today, by grace.
pt>en:23856426351c1d34: Sex and the supremacy of Christ
pt>en:13b2db1104ae163b: God made sex to reveal something
pt>en:44099c40ab37edc8: Sex and the Supremacy of Christ (org. com Justin Taylor, 2005)
pt>en:e68672558d350ac3: John Piper and Justin Taylor organized a book with lectures by various pastors on sexuality. The title sums up Piper's thesis: sex, like everything in life, exists for the glory of Christ. When Christ is the greatest treasure, sex finds its right place.
pt>en:ef6d1dc29e355630: For those who have already fallen, Piper reminds us that the cross is enough. Guilt doesn't have to be the last word. The same Christ who forgives is what gives strength to start over. Purity is the fruit of grace, not a trophy for those who never erred.
pt>en:c2c2452edf6e13f7: Piper argues that God created sexuality to teach us about it. The union of marriage is an image of the union between Christ and the church (Ephesians 5:31–32). Conjugal fidelity shows the fidelity of Christ. Therefore, when sex is used outside God's design, He tells a lie about the gospel itself.
pt>en:0e420068332e60fe: Piper is realistic: sexual temptation is strong, especially in a world saturated with images. He does not offer tricks, but a strategy of faith. Sexual sin promises pleasure; the answer is not just to say "no," but to find greater pleasure in God. It is the logic he calls Christian hedonism: we fight against false pleasures with the promise of higher joys.
pt>en:041a72e8e2269291: Pure and Simple Christianity (Mere Christianity, 1952), chapter on sexual morality
pt>en:1a69f0c36404f115: Lewis makes an important observation: the sins of the flesh are serious, but not the worst. Pride, cruelty, and a cold spirit of judgment can be more dangerous. This protects against a hypocritical morality that condemns others and ignores one's own heart.
pt>en:daa2c7c3a9d5c23b: C. S. Lewis was not reformed. He was Anglican, a literature professor at Oxford and Cambridge, and author of The Chronicles of Narnia. But his chapter on sexual morality in Pure and Simple Christianity is cited by Christians of many traditions, including Reformed, for the clarity with which it addresses the subject.
pt>en:13fba66f3a275974: The Reformed tradition agrees with Lewis on the standard and adds emphasis on grace: we do not attain chastity only through effort, but through the work of the Spirit in those united to Christ. Lewis himself ends by saying that when we fall, we must get up and start over, asking God for help. Purity is a path of continuous repentance and hope.
pt>en:ba9d49a658682a02: To illustrate, Lewis makes a famous comparison. Imagine a country where people fill theaters to see someone slowly lift the lid of a plate, showing a piece of meat. pt>en:bca2534ff66080a2: Emanuel does not mean "God solves everything," nor "God explains everything." It means "God with us." Sometimes we pray asking for answers, and He offers us presence. It seems little until we discover that it is everything. A child scared in the dark does not want a lesson about electricity; it wants the father in the bedroom.
pt>en:9f4b86a1b80a7751: David wanted to build a house for God. God replied that he, God, would build a house for David. Our best plans for God are almost always less than his plans for us. Mature faith learns to receive a "no" that comes wrapped in "something greater."
pt>en:52e3e38ef39dbe14: Are you more concerned with doing something for God or letting Him do something in you?
pt>en:867e77b9c5f1a5fb: Where do you need a star to guide your walk now?
pt>en:cf8e5c8c82765b3c: In what situation this week do you need to remember that you are not alone?
pt>en:862b6ca24a59c0da: What would it mean today simply to let the light come?
pt>en:c7d892a330abfc96: What dark area of your life have you been trying to illuminate with your own strength?
pt>en:884a7f063b2e0f62: Isaiah does not say that the people came out of darkness to find the light. He says that the light shone upon those who walked in darkness. The initiative is entirely from God. How many times do we think we need to find the way on our own? The Gospel is the news that the light has come to us.
pt>en:3705175833956c29: The titles are enormous: Counselor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace. And the package is tiny: a boy. God likes to hide infinity in small things. Maybe that's why so many people pass by him without realizing it. Those who expect noisy greatness may lose the glory that cries in a cradle.
pt>en:3a1580bfec97e517: Of the four names in Isaiah 9:6, which one do you need to know most now?
pt>en:3035459dd0de2c8a: Can you trust that God works at the roots even when nothing appears on the surface?
pt>en:8bee1cfec495a9b0: A cut stump seems like the end of the story. No one photographs a stump. But Isaiah sees a sprout there. David's lineage was reduced to almost nothing when God sprouted the Messiah. There are hopes in you that seem cut close to the ground. God is an expert in roots that no one else sees.
pt>en:d347d8ffb46a972a: Who around you needs to hear a true word of comfort this week?
pt>en:f7011630f3602d3d: What dream or prayer seems like a dry stump in your life today?
pt>en:4f97c767441c830f: Have you been despising the small, quiet ways God acts in your life?
pt>en:6317b32131a4fa7b: Do you tend to see God more as strong and distant or as tender and fragile?
pt>en:54173bdcba5e2603: Where in your life do you need to be carried instead of trying to walk alone?
pt>en:f2245b27c8196756: After thirty-nine chapters of judgment, Isaiah opens with "Comfort." God's discipline is never the final word. But notice: the consolation does not ignore sin, it declares that the debt has been paid. Cheap consolation says "it was nothing." True consolation says "it was serious, and it has already been resolved."
pt>en:db115a34d11e5dd2: The same arm that governs with power carries the lambs in its lap. We like to separate things: a strong God for big problems, a tender God for tears. Isaiah brings the two together in a single image. God's strength does not make him distant, and His tenderness does not make him weak.
pt>en:5d457dfc5e3fc461: Have you accepted God's comfort or do you keep punishing yourself for something already forgiven?
pt>en:c4b213c3f064d6ee: What pain or guilt of yours have you not yet handed over to the one who has already taken it?
pt>en:48214c16ea3a4300: How does remembering the cross change the way you will live this Christmas?
pt>en:ff95e2d03492276c: Do you still try to present your own righteousness to God?
pt>en:69e046d9b6c8b2e8: Where have you felt too small to be used by God?
pt>en:1ef087f6c56291bc: What would it be like to rest today in the righteousness of Christ instead of His performance?
pt>en:bc5029c2b6decb83: Bethlehem was too small to be on the list of important cities. God placed it at the center of history. He does this often: He chooses the insignificant to shame what is considered great. If you feel small, you are in great company. God likes to start with places like this.
pt>en:def705198ffcc177: Read slowly the verbs: taken, taken, pierced, ground up. All active for him, all in our favor. Christmas is not a cute story about a baby; it is the beginning of the path to the cross. The manger and the wood are made from the same wood of grace.
pt>en:19b1859c030bb33e: The name is bold: "The Lord, Our Righteousness." Not "the Lord who helps us to be just," but the very righteousness placed in our account. This topples the pride of those who think they are good and lifts the heads of those who feel lost. No one is left out because they are too sinful, nor do they enter because they are good enough.
pt>en:64dcf6337eda5492: When was the last time your faith tasted joy and not just duty?
pt>en:2580596a16285080: Before the King comes the messenger. Before the meeting, the prepared path. God rarely arrives by surprise at a heart that has not been flattened. Preparing the way is not winning the visit; it is removing from the midst the stones that prevent arrival. Advent is a season of inner cleaning.
pt>en:34211f0e9099206e: What could you remove from your schedule to make room for God?
pt>en:d65b2850d537f4b7: What "stone" in your life is hindering the arrival of Christ this Christmas?
pt>en:0711b55b1a391114: Malachi imagines calves loose from the pen, jumping for joy. It's an almost funny image for such a serious prophet. But that's how the Old Testament ends: with the promise of a healing sun. After that, four hundred years of silence. The promise hung in the air, waiting for dawn.
pt>en:742380bdeba80bbf: How would your view of "unimportant" people change if you thought of Bethlehem?
pt>en:bba441ba1244d82a: Is there a prayer you keep saying but no longer expect to be answered?
pt>en:3307979bf694e9ca: What could silence teach you in this noisy time?
pt>en:d03245bc4b55ab7e: Zacharias spent years praying for a son. When the answer finally came, he doubted. It's strange, but it's human: sometimes we pray so long that we stop waiting. God left him in silence for nine months. Perhaps silence was the best school: there he learned to listen before speaking.
pt>en:7b23019d41a62b26: What fear has kept you from saying yes to what God is asking?
pt>en:b38796a84abdad41: What wound would you like the Sun of Justice to touch this Advent?
pt>en:9db575f8af65bb34: Can you move forward with unanswered questions, like Maria?
pt>en:7bd6cc5eb3a7a570: Have you conditioned your obedience to understand all the details first?
pt>en:83eee2923fe5b7e4: "Let it be done to me according to your word." Few sentences were so short and cost so much. Mary risked her reputation, her engagement, and perhaps her life. True surrender is rarely comfortable. She does not say "I have understood everything," she says "I trust in the one who calls me."
pt>en:de8eb903baf6a249: Can you praise God for something He promised but has not yet happened?
pt>en:a8fb5094abec5815: Mary sings before seeing anything. There was still no belly, no cradle, no angels in heaven. Only a promise. Her worship is born from trust, not circumstances. We like to praise after victory. Mary teaches us to praise at the beginning of the story, when everything is still promise.
pt>en:ad0989a838c6bdac: The angel begins with "Do not be afraid." Every time God approaches, it seems He needs to calm us first. It makes sense: the holy presence is frightening. But fear does not need to have the last word. Mary did not receive all the answers; she received the assurance that God was in command.
pt>en:4a854b7fc2bfa83c: If you wrote your own "Magnificat" today, what would you say?
pt>en:211f63cf3bd40451: What would your "do it in me" be today?
pt>en:14a35438a88fdcb5: Is your faith more evident in your words or actions?
pt>en:1f3721d23582d5ff: What step of obedience have you been postponing, waiting for a clearer signal?
pt>en:5267754ebfd2e058: At what recent moment did you realize that God visited you?
pt>en:8c752fce47317849: What "shadow of death" in your life needs the light of dawn?
pt>en:158d9d2ef7a427ac: Zacharias, after nine months silent, opens his mouth and sings about the dawn. Those who have passed through silence usually see the light better. The expression is beautiful: God visited us. He did not send a message, He came personally. Advent is this: the God who knocks at your door.
pt>en:76cf70b7085bc35a: The Bible does not record a single word from Joseph. None. Only obedience. He woke up and did what God commanded. In a culture that values those who speak loudest, Joseph is a reminder that character is revealed in what we do when no one is applauding.
pt>en:0b5287b8f79a7a33: What is occupying the space that should belong to Christ this Christmas?
pt>en:64ac9269da0d7e6e: What concrete place will you open for him this week?
pt>en:114baa94914f3142: Have you ever felt like you lack credentials to receive good news from God?
pt>en:48f7adc00e3c4011: The first news of Christmas was not for the priests nor for the palace. It was for shepherds on the night shift, people who smelled like sheep and had no voice in the courts. God chose the despised as the first witnesses. The joy of the Gospel does not ask for badges of importance.
pt>en:647a8141c75c1691: Who are the "night shift pastors" around you who need to hear this joy?
pt>en:69ad7135f77cfa10: The whole sky sings about a child who has not yet performed any miracle. The glory of God does not depend on visible results. On Christmas night, it is worth stopping and asking: what kind of peace is this that the angels proclaim? It is not the absence of problems, it is the presence of God among them.
pt>en:acc69a7469737a09: There was no room. The phrase bothers because it is still relevant. There is no room in the busy schedule, in the busy heart, in the noisy December house. The problem with the guesthouse was not malice, it was overcrowding. Maybe ours is too. Christ is rarely expelled; almost always he is just squeezed out.
pt>en:0f3879abf913a6fa: On this Christmas Eve, what is taking away your peace?
pt>en:42524c6270b78710: What would it be like to give glory to God before seeing everything resolved?
pt>en:3e0b5e1eb1874c4b: What does it mean to you today that God wanted to live nearby?
pt>en:6fd52ac32196c441: John does not begin his Gospel with a barn or shepherds. He begins with eternity: in the beginning was the Word. And then, in a sentence, the eternal enters time. God did not cry out from heaven; He pitched His tent among us. Christmas is God's courage to stay close to people like us.
pt>en:0aa2e783ccd4b2b7: On this festive day, how can you be the presence of Christ to someone who is lonely?
pt>en:4b2b4d1d14e874dd: What do you think you need to have to be at peace?
pt>en:0de9f9ea4ce0832f: Simeon waited his whole life for an encounter. When he held the boy, he said: now I can leave in peace. He didn't ask for more time, more things, or more achievements. It was enough to see Jesus. There is enormous freedom in discovering that what is essential is not what we accumulate, but who we find.
pt>en:9c680d299c15acb2: If you had seen what Simeon saw, what would it not matter so much?
pt>en:61b3eac1a61bd262: Hannah had every reason for bitterness: early widowhood, decades of waiting, old age. Instead, she chose the temple, prayer, and hope. We do not choose everything that happens to us, but we choose where we will live inside. Hannah lived in the house of God.
pt>en:82af8ab85ec8ff7c: What can you learn from someone older whose faith has withstood the test of time?
pt>en:d5dc00120d9cc0cf: How much has your worship cost you?
pt>en:c372bb856cdc5105: After this Christmas, by which "other path" does God want you to return?
pt>en:c854d7e49536bd65: Where have you lived inside: in bitterness or in hope?
pt>en:b118d7dd610f61a8: Have you confused the presence of God with the absence of difficulties?
pt>en:94dbef0e392e4b2a: In what situation do you need God's guidance to cross, not to escape?
pt>en:e6b61732b98b6b25: The Magi traveled a lot for a baby who didn't even speak. Educated people, from another culture, who knelt. True worship always costs something: time, distance, pride. And they returned by another path. Those who truly meet Jesus do not return the same way.
pt>en:67c60dd641764a46: Right after the choir of angels comes the nighttime flight into Egypt. Christmas did not end with lights, but with danger. This is consolation for those who discover that being at the center of God's will does not mean being far from trouble. God did not avoid Herod's threat; He guided the family into it.
pt>en:91bbc5cc9d66c2d1: "In the fullness of time." God was neither late nor early. His clock is different from ours, but it is never broken. And the goal was not only to forgive us, it was to adopt us. A judge can acquit a defendant and send him home. God acquits and takes the defendant to live with Him.
pt>en:2e1db89e9af8ba1c: Do you relate to God more as a forgiven defendant or as an adopted son?
pt>en:e929cad21e19b7cb: What do you expect to be delivered to God's clock this year-end?
pt>en:73f11b53b1f67749: On the last day of the year, the Bible shows us the last page of history: a city without the need for sun, because the Lamb is the light. Every end of the year brings balance and longing. But those who know the end of the story can go through any difficult chapter without despair.
pt>en:1c5b922586bb3ce7: Looking ahead to this year, where did you see God's light shine?
pt>en:f3f7c8cb065615c4: What hope do you want to carry with you into the coming year?
pt>en:53f198a7b51b3ef7: Neither legalism nor libertinism: the whole Christ
pt>en:770718e69527130f: Two deviations with the same root
pt>en:114d407152ac7270: The law in the right place
pt>en:f00974bdc6c9bba6: Certainty that it is born from the gospel
pt>en:cd9c2ac4e5075df0: Free from all, servant of all
pt>en:4817fe959feed824: Sinclair Ferguson, a Scottish pastor and theology professor, wrote a book that starts from an ancient controversy in eighteenth-century Scotland, known as the Marrow controversy. The discussion seems distant, but it touches on a question every Christian faces: how do grace, law, and the certainty of salvation relate?
pt>en:4e08bd8c13f702d5: Ferguson shows that legalism and antinomianism, which is the rejection of the law in the Christian life, seem opposed, but they arise from the same place. Both separate the benefits of Christ from the person of Christ. The legalist wants the blessing, but thinks he needs to pay for it. The antinomian wants forgiveness, but does not want the Lord who offers it. In both, God is seen as a suspicious patron, not as a generous Father.
pt>en:53f6d31027fbe07e: A God who is not a hostage
pt>en:5f5f64be8f6eea35: Search: A. W. Pink, The Sovereignty of God
pt>en:1fc750659591f92f: Read Daniel 4 this week. Then, write a concern that has kept you awake at night and, next to it, the phrase: the Most High has dominion. Pray to hand this situation over to Him, with trust and reverence.
pt>en:051dd9c34ae8f626: Arthur W. Pink was an English pastor and writer who spent much of his life away from the spotlight, writing Bible studies for a small group of readers. One of his books, however, survived the century and is still read worldwide: a passionate defense that God is, in fact, God.
pt>en:bb387460c7b8bdd9: Pink insisted that this doctrine was not given to fuel cold discussions. It humbles pride because it shows that we depend on God in everything. And it comforts the afflicted, because it assures that even pain is in the hands of a wise Father. As Nebuchadnezzar learned, no one can stop God's hand or ask Him: what are you doing?
pt>en:5681278ea80c1d92: Pink was troubled by a common idea in his time: that of a well-intentioned but weak God who desires many things and depends on human goodwill to accomplish them. For him, this is not the God of the Bible. The Lord of the Scriptures does everything that pleases Him, in heaven and on earth. Nothing catches Him by surprise, nothing defeats Him, nothing escapes His rule.
pt>en:c4c69b7c2013b9d5: The book passes through nature, history, angels, and men, and reaches salvation. Pink shows that grace is not an offering God leaves on the table hoping someone will be interested. It is God Himself who chooses, calls, regenerates, and keeps His own. This does not nullify human responsibility, but it takes away from us the merit.
pt>en:bc1e3562a73489a2: Jerry Bridges served for decades in the missionary organization Navegantes and became known for writing about the Christian life with simplicity and depth. In one of his most widely read books, he addresses a question every believer faces sooner or later: how to trust God when life hurts?
pt>en:b7bb512f3c2d8ead: Today, if you catch yourself thinking that God only accepts you when you are well, stop and read Titus 2 slowly. There, the same grace that saves also educates. Receive Christ again, whole, and obey as a child, not as an employee.
pt>en:76deea424855756f: The remedy is to receive Christ Himself, whole, freely offered in the gospel. In Him we have justification and sanctification, forgiveness and new life, without one thing separating from the other. No one needs to first become good enough to come to Him. The invitation is for sinners as sinners.
pt>en:246cb8628f463db0: Bridges reminds us that trusting is also a decision. In dark times, we choose to believe what God said, not what fear suggests. This choice is nourished by the Word, prayer, and the memory of past faithfulness.
pt>en:1b4cc00e8ab669e9: Many believers live insecure because they look too much at themselves. Ferguson points outward: certainty is born from contemplating God's grace in Christ and His promises. The fruits confirm, but the foundation is the Savior.
pt>en:6c6f288d9d9ae50c: Bridges sums up the path in three biblical statements. God is completely sovereign: nothing happens outside His control. God is infinite in wisdom: He knows what is best, even when we don't. And God is perfect in love: everything He does with His own is born from His care. If one of these three truths falls, trust collapses. Together, they sustain us.
pt>en:946bb33e3db62966: One of the strongest lessons from the book is that trust does not depend on explanation. Often we will not know why something happened. Bridges does not promise answers for every tear. He points to the character of God revealed in Scripture. We may not understand God's hand, but we can trust His heart.
pt>en:4fed76dad586a52b: Ferguson reminds us that the law is not the enemy of the believer. It does not save us, but it reveals the character of God and describes the life of love that the Spirit produces. Those who have been reached by grace begin to love what they once feared. Obedience ceases to be a price and becomes gratitude.
pt>en:f94b0882bd9b1d00: Learning to pray with the apostle Paul
pt>en:69b48c2e6fececc8: The prayer and glory of God
pt>en:9d91d31c2fe7637e: Pink's conclusion is practical: a sovereign God deserves to be feared, obeyed, and worshipped. Prayer gains strength because we speak to those who can act. Obedience gains joy because we serve those who do not fail.
pt>en:39e22d0a8b499d37: D. A. Carson in The Gospel Coalition
pt>en:1c79bb8852d434f3: Paul begins many letters thanking God for his brothers. Carson shows that this shapes the heart. Those who give thanks for other Christians learn to see God's grace working in them, even with their flaws, and pray with more love and less criticism.
pt>en:938ea24af59becbb: The author shows that God's sovereignty is not only about big events. It reaches the small things: a diagnosis, a lost job, a decision by another person that affects us. Even the wrong actions of others do not escape God's government, who is able to turn them into good for those who love Him, as He did with Joseph.
pt>en:b0f08e4ed4f7440d: As he studies Paul's prayers, Carson notices something that confronts us. Paul rarely prays for health, finances, or circumstances, although these things are not forbidden. He prays that the brothers may know God better, grow in love, understand the hope of the calling, and live in a way worthy of the Lord. Our request lists are usually quite different.
pt>en:6775c3678260079a: Don Carson, a New Testament scholar, noticed that many churches talk a lot about prayer but pray little and poorly. His proposal was simple and profound: if we want to renew our prayer life, we need to learn from the prayers God recorded in the Bible, especially those of the apostle Paul.
pt>en:0d686c5e4310eadf: Search: Paul Miller, A Praying Life
pt>en:d296ff127c51e055: Paul Miller wrote about prayer from ordinary life: a large family, a daughter with a disability, full days, and fatigue. He does not speak as someone who masters the subject, but as someone who has learned, slowly, to depend on God. That is why so many readers recognize themselves in what he writes.
pt>en:800223322c69cbe4: Take a notebook or your cell phone today and write down three concrete requests for your family. Pray for them with simple words, like a child would speak to their father. In a month, return to the list and see what God has done, including what He has changed in you.
pt>en:1a84381b8b3327c2: For the author, feeling weak is not an obstacle to praying; it is the very invitation. Those who think they can do it alone do not pray. Prayer is born when we recognize that we cannot take care of children, marriage, work, or our own heart. Helplessness, given to God, becomes faith.
pt>en:78a740e2ea88e3ed: Miller notes that many Christians don't pray because they think they first need to get their mind and heart right. But children don't do that. They come to the Father as they are, talking about everything at once. Jesus teaches us to call God Father. Prayer begins when we stop pretending and go to Him with our mess.
pt>en:c5ee0f910f38ec7b: Finally, Miller shows that praying is not just a separate moment, but an ongoing conversation. Small prayers in traffic, in the kitchen, or before a meeting keep the heart turned toward the Father.
pt>en:1c7a2a2218732b10: Miller also deals with a silent enemy: cynicism. After prayers that seem unanswered, the heart learns to be suspicious. It calls us to remember that God is writing a bigger story, and that often only afterwards do we see how He responded. Writing down requests and answers helps us perceive God's hand.
pt>en:0590758cbd0677c8: Choose a verse from Romans 8 today and repeat it throughout the day, especially when anxiety is tight. Tell God sincerely: I don't understand, but I trust in you. This simple prayer is also faith.
pt>en:2fb31db9b4c4eea5: In the end, Carson reminds us that the purpose of prayer is not to get God to do our will, but to align our hearts with his. Praying Paul's prayers is learning to desire what God desires: that Christ be known and loved.
pt>en:67a465ff7203e3e5: Kevin DeYoung at The Gospel Coalition
pt>en:b72a803cd9626b83: A greater love drives out the lesser
pt>en:2cebc5354c006c5d: Choose this week a specific sin you have tolerated. Confess it to God, ask a mature brother for help, and decide on a practical step to escape it. Do this with hope: the same God who called you is the one who will complete the work.
pt>en:8e75c0c52126ca8e: The Expulsive Power of a New Affection (sermon The Expulsive Power of a New Affection)
pt>en:b95279f5c8e8096f: One common fear is that talking about effort contradicts grace. DeYoung answers that grace is not opposed to effort, but to merit. Paul commands salvation to be developed with fear and trembling, because it is God who works in us. The Christian fights, prays, reads, flees temptation, and does good, but does all this supported by the work of Christ and the power of the Spirit.
pt>en:526327b92c0183f8: Kevin DeYoung, a Presbyterian pastor in the United States, noticed a curious gap in the church of his time. Many Christians speak enthusiastically about grace, gospel, and social justice, but little about personal holiness. It seems the topic has become outdated or dangerous. For him, this is a hole that needs to be filled.
pt>en:c4a4d0d476d1d75d: DeYoung insists that growth is often slow and common. It comes through the Word, through prayer, through fellowship in church, through the Lord's Supper, and through confession. There are no spectacular shortcuts, but there is God's faithfulness.
pt>en:8cc1d2d6c732e548: Why banning alone is not enough
pt>en:3699d6229da29308: DeYoung reminds us that the Bible does not treat holiness as an extra for more dedicated Christians. Without it, Hebrews says, no one will see the Lord. This does not mean we are saved for being holy, but that those who have been saved are called and empowered to grow in holiness. God did not save us to leave us as we were.
pt>en:c680c1da7d7a584f: This week, read Colossians 1:9-12 and use this prayer for three people in your church, one per day. Change their names in the text and ask God to give them knowledge of His will, fruits, and joy. Then, tell one of them that you prayed.
pt>en:8f521b12c34a67cf: This changes the way we seek holiness. Besides watching and resisting, we need to contemplate Christ in the Scriptures, in prayer, and in worship. His beauty is the best remedy against the charms of sin.
pt>en:a606bdd554c845e3: Thomas Chalmers was a pastor, teacher, and church leader in 19th-century Scotland. Among many sermons, one became famous for its title and its idea: the force that expels love for the world from the heart is a new, stronger love. This simple intuition helps greatly in the fight against sin.
pt>en:dd999d0b1108f77d: Search: Thomas Chalmers, The Expulsive Power of a New Affection
pt>en:307107d360f42cbe: Chalmers notes that the human heart cannot stand a vacuum. It always loves something. Therefore, just showing that something is bad rarely makes someone give it up. We can know that a habit harms us and remain attached to it, because the heart does not want to be left without anything to love.
pt>en:e7542fb683cb2b88: Many try to overcome sin only with willpower and rules. Chalmers does not despise God's law, but shows that it alone does not change desires. Tearing away one love without putting another in its place is like trying to empty a bottle at the bottom of the sea: as soon as the water comes out, another comes in. What expels an affection is a greater affection.
pt>en:1c3893167ed62286: And what is this greater love? Chalmers points to the gospel. When we see God as He revealed Himself in Christ, full of grace and truth, the heart begins to be drawn. The world loses its brightness not because we close our eyes to Him, but because we open our eyes to something more beautiful. John says that whoever loves the world does not have the Father's love; the opposite is also true.
pt>en:344511a75828ab8c: Carson says that prayer does not happen by chance. Those who expect to want to pray rarely pray. That's why he recommends planning: set aside some time, use lists, pray quietly or aloud so as not to get distracted, and mix worship, confession, gratitude, and requests. Discipline does not kill spontaneity; it opens space for fellowship to grow.
pt>en:6fd1278228eb9989: Married to God, not just to each other
pt>en:599bf3c29f2c4bf9: Another beautiful point of the book is that God can rejoice in the obedience of His children. Our works do not buy the Father's love, but He delights in them as a father delights in the footsteps of the little son. This frees us both from arrogance and from the feeling that nothing we do matters.
pt>en:36752ad75c1e7b4a: Search: Christopher Ash, Married for God
pt>en:166051de2aa231d5: Ash also speaks of exclusivity and the permanence of the alliance. Sexual fidelity and the promise until death are not prisons, but walls of protection so that love grows in safety.
pt>en:a81fe4ca00486435: Talk today with your spouse about a question: how can our marriage serve God and others this month? Choose a concrete gesture together, such as hosting someone for a meal or helping a church family.
pt>en:d61862f834a543fc: Ash reminds us that marriage was not invented by us. It was born in the garden, by God's hands, before the fall. Therefore, its meaning does not depend on fads or passing feelings. The one who created marriage is the one who defines what it is for, and the Bible shows that it exists, above all, for the glory of God.
pt>en:85d05c7cdc692447: When marriage exists only for the satisfaction of both, it closes off and gets tired. When it exists to serve God, love gains direction. The couple stops asking only if they are happy and starts asking how they can, together, be faithful and useful. Curiously, this is how many find deeper joy.
pt>en:4d4d2590a56fd59a: What the Puritans knew about the home
pt>en:ca528c4d9c2a045b: Christopher Ash, pastor and teacher in England, wrote about marriage from an uncommon question. Instead of starting with what marriage can do for me, he asks why God created marriage. The shift in focus seems small, but it transforms everything.
pt>en:7dbd4ef586e53503: When temptation comes this week, don't just think about not doing it. Think about whom you love most. Read 1 John 2, give thanks for the Father's love, and ask the Spirit to take the place that sin wants to take.
pt>en:3eefe8340d4003dc: Worldly Saints: The Puritans as They Really Were, 1986)
pt>en:ec60d85cf2fb527c: The house as a small church
pt>en:eae143546c1e41c5: Ryken does not idealize the Puritans; they also had flaws. But his vision challenges a culture that separates faith from life from home. What they remind us is that the most common place, the kitchen, the table, and the living room, can be a place of worship.
pt>en:271fd32a14424ba1: In Genesis 2, God gives man a task: to cultivate and guard the garden. The woman is called the helper who corresponds to her. Ash emphasizes that this word does not indicate inferiority; God himself is called the helper of Israel. Husband and wife are partners in the work God entrusted to them: caring for the world, serving others, receiving and raising children when God gives them, and opening the house to the kingdom.
pt>en:e271da21b458f866: The Puritans spoke of authority and submission at home, but Ryken emphasizes that they always linked this to love and mutual service. The husband's authority existed to care, not to dominate. Children should honor their parents, and parents should treat their children with patience and wisdom.
pt>en:5cff15256e73a064: Start this week with something simple: a short Bible reading and a prayer after dinner, at least three times. It doesn't have to last long. Let Colossians 3 be the first text, and ask God that the peace of Christ will govern your home.
pt>en:75db8a33f0d120c5: A common image among them was that of the family as a small church. The home was a place of prayer, Bible reading, catechism, and singing. The father was responsible for conducting this domestic service, but the whole house participated. It was not formality, but rather about putting God at the center of the routine.
pt>en:08a5846866ec527f: Leland Ryken, a literature professor in the United States, decided to undo a caricature. Many imagine Puritans as cold, sad, and anti-pleasure people. While studying his writings, Ryken found something else: people who took faith and common life seriously, including marriage and family.
pt>en:f2375fce6c17e988: Parents who teach faith at home
pt>en:3340dd9b2479f6bd: Ryken shows that the Puritans reacted to a view that placed celibacy above marriage. For them, marriage was a holy and good vocation, created by God. Their preachers spoke of the love between husband and wife with warmth and beauty, calling the spouse companion and friend. Affection was not a detail, but a duty and a joy.
pt>en:e30497ccb2ee5ec2: A generation that is drifting apart
pt>en:638c54731cb5060d: Baucham values the local church and advocates that it support parents rather than take their place. Pastors and teachers help, but the home is the first missionary field.
pt>en:6255839075a6383b: Voddie Baucham, a reformed Baptist pastor and preacher known in the United States and Africa, wrote a book that upset many Christian parents. His thesis is clear: the main responsibility for the spiritual formation of children does not lie with Sunday school or youth ministry, but with the father and mother.
pt>en:e4aa3f3b193ba2ef: The central text of the book is God's command to Israel: to love the Lord with all your heart and speak His words while sitting at home, walking along the road, lying down, and getting up. Baucham shows that faith is transmitted in everyday life. Conversations at the table, in the car, and before bedtime are opportunities for discipleship.
pt>en:a5a3c90367c041bf: Choose a fixed time this week to open Deuteronomy 6 with your children. Read some verses, ask a simple question about the text, and pray together. If you don't have children, pray for a family in your church and offer help to tired parents.
pt>en:8c2614384e99e8f4: Search: Voddie Baucham, Family Driven Faith
pt>en:b933ad65ff6d0ae7: Baucham begins with a real concern. Many young people raised in the church abandon the faith when they leave home. He doesn't blame only the culture. He asks if the parents haven't outsourced what God entrusted to them. Taking the children to worship is good, but it doesn't replace teaching the faith in daily life.
pt>en:cbf51552e03a2eb7: Giving grace to children, not just rules
pt>en:e71c66edcabd2ac9: The law and the gospel at home
pt>en:59596fbe43c5b95d: One of the most liberating points of the book is that parents don't need to pretend to be perfect. When they make mistakes, they can ask their children for forgiveness. This shows, in practice, that everyone in the house lives with the same mercy.
pt>en:8defa0fd8163a84b: Finally, the authors remind us that the salvation of children does not depend on the parents' technique. We are called to be faithful, but it is God who changes hearts. This truth takes a huge burden off our shoulders.
pt>en:00627b5fe6f6abcc: The authors warn of a subtle danger. We can raise educated, obedient, and morally correct children who never understood they need a Savior. When the main message of home is to be good and God will love you, we teach a religion of merit. The Bible shows another way: we are loved because Christ was good in our place.
pt>en:5bbf2d07bbe00e69: This does not mean abandoning rules. God's law shows what is right and reveals sin, including that of children. But after correcting, parents should point to Christ, who forgives and transforms. Discipline, then, is not just punishment; it is an occasion to remind the child that they need grace, as both father and mother do.
pt>en:63d46aadfe2122c3: Search: Elyse Fitzpatrick, Give Them Grace
pt>en:ca43b6dcdd81a708: The next time you need to correct your child, end the conversation by talking about Jesus: his forgiveness and the love that does not change. Read Ephesians 6:4 and ask God not to provoke your children to anger, but to raise them in the discipline and care of the Lord.
pt>en:fe5d9b5e667ec083: Elyse Fitzpatrick, a Bible counselor, wrote this book together with her daughter, Jessica Thompson, who at the time was raising her own children. Mother and daughter looked honestly at how many Christian parents educate: with good rules, good examples, and little gospel. Their proposal is to place grace at the center of raising children.
pt>en:f1abd13b1421ccd6: Running Scared: Fear, Worry, and the God of Rest (2007)
pt>en:2d248cc409d48a09: A kingdom that does not shake
pt>en:630575c92d8401ff: Edward Welch, a biblical counselor and psychologist by training, spent years listening to anxious people. Instead of treating fear just as a problem to be eliminated, he sees it as a window to the heart. Fear reveals what we love and what we trust.
pt>en:5b7e534a70920558: Welch ends by pointing to the kingdom of God. When the heart first seeks the kingdom, other things take their place. We do not stop taking care of responsibilities, but we begin to do so with rest.
pt>en:a16cf42db01d2662: Strong castle in times of fear
pt>en:31525b287dce31e8: Anthem Strong Castle is Our God (Ein feste Burg ist unser Gott)
pt>en:77bede0d66d8c7cf: The good news is that God responds to fear with words. One of the most repeated phrases in the Bible is do not fear. Welch shows that this command never comes alone. It comes accompanied by a promise: I am with you, I am your God, I help you. God does not command us to be courageous on our own, but calls us to trust in His presence.
pt>en:6a083e30a3b766e6: Welch notes that we care about what is important to us: children, health, money, reputation, the future. Fear is like a voice that says: you will lose something you need. Listening to that voice carefully helps us realize where the heart is supported. Sometimes we find that we place our security in things that cannot sustain it.
pt>en:e78a65fd3c61de05: An important lesson from the book is that of manna. God fed Israel in the desert with enough for one day at a time. Anxiety tries to live tomorrow ahead of time. Jesus teaches us to ask for today's bread and to leave tomorrow in the Father's hands. Grace comes in the measure of the day.
pt>en:c03477fbb239c931: When worry tightens today, ask: what am I afraid to lose? Then, read Matthew 6:25-34 and turn worry into a request. If anxiety is intense and constant, also seek help from a pastor and a health professional; this is not a lack of faith.
pt>en:54f90c8999f1c12b: The enemy has already been judged
pt>en:1b2e5d33a902f504: In the final stanza, Luther says they can take possessions, honor, family, and even life, but the kingdom of God remains. This is not disdain for good things, but the certainty that, in Christ, nothing eternal can be taken from us.
pt>en:990982b40c51c9da: Psalm 46 begins by saying that God is refuge and strength, a help very present in tribulations. Luther turned this truth into an image: a strong castle, where the persecuted takes shelter. Fear makes us seek shelter in many places. The hymn reminds us that only God is a truly safe place.
pt>en:afcfe0698d2026fd: Children learn more from what they see than from what they hear. That is why the author challenges parents to examine their own hearts. A father who loves the Word, however, asks for forgiveness and treats his wife with honor teaches more than many lessons. True faith begins in the heart of the one who teaches.
pt>en:5d9a6833e9f5f2f9: When God weeps with those who weep
pt>en:2d32dd862dd209ba: Read Psalm 46 aloud today and, if you can, sing or listen to Strong Castle. Then, repeat verse 10 for a few minutes in silence: be quiet and know that I am God. Give him the fear that weighs most now.
pt>en:63e4c19814172479: Joni Eareckson Tada became quadriplegic at seventeen after diving in shallow water. Since then, she has lived in a wheelchair and served people with disabilities around the world. In this book, written with Pastor Steven Estes, she addresses suffering not as a theory, but as someone who carries it every day.
pt>en:0ce0613086af4f56: Joni speaks joyfully of the hope of the resurrection. She looks forward to the day when she will dance with new legs. The present afflictions, Paul says, produce an eternal weight of glory. This does not lessen the pain, but places it within a larger story.
pt>en:5e1d97f79c2bfddf: The center of the book is the cross. God does not watch pain from afar. In Christ, He entered into suffering, was wounded, abandoned, and killed. The God who governs is the same who weeps. That is why we can trust that He understands us and that He turns even the worst wounds into instruments of grace.
pt>en:128849f48164eff3: If you are suffering, read 2 Corinthians 4:16-18 slowly and tell God, sincerely, what hurts. If you know someone who is suffering, visit that person this week. Speak little, listen a lot, and pray with them.
pt>en:3cea00d14fc09147: The authors state, with reformed faith, that nothing escapes God's government, not even suffering. This may seem harsh at first glance. But they show that the alternative would be much worse: a world where pain happens senselessly and without control. Because God reigns, suffering has limits and purpose, even when we don't understand it.
pt>en:ecb361dc472c2292: Joni does not hide that he struggled with God. There were phases of revolt, depression, and unanswered questions. The book does not offer ready-made phrases. It begins by acknowledging that pain is real and that the Bible does not ask us to pretend everything is okay. The lamenting psalms show that we can lead God to our complaint.
pt>en:e4bc7301e52fabf5: Few hymns have been sung as much in church history as Castle Forte, written by Martin Luther from Psalm 46. Luther knew fear firsthand: death threats, illness, family losses, and intense spiritual struggles. His hymn was not born from a quiet life, but from a faith that learned to take refuge in God.
pt>en:ca28097274a20772: The hymn speaks of the devil as a terrible and cunning enemy. Luther does not minimize evil. But he states that one word alone is enough to overthrow it. Christ's victory on the cross and in the resurrection means that evil will not have the last word. Therefore, we can face fear without being dominated by it.
pt>en:701da86a24989eee: Luther sings honestly that, with our strength, we can do nothing; soon we would be lost. This is liberating. Faith does not require us to be strong. It invites us to admit weakness and look to the one who fights for us. In the hymn, this defender has a name: Jesus Christ, the Lord of hosts.
pt>en:9b82f31fbddcd7a2: The God who works in pain
pt>en:5caf0237ed3806ca: Another mark of the letters is the longing for heaven. Rutherford wrote as someone who already smelled the scent of glory. That hope gave strength to remain faithful, even far from home and the pulpit.
pt>en:5f65cdd3ca932c4f: Many letters were written to parents who lost children and to widows. Rutherford did not despise tears. He cried with those who wept. But he also remembered that those who die in the Lord are not lost; they went only ahead, to the Father's house. The separation is real, but temporary.
pt>en:344da2a382d8ac2a: Rutherford saw God's hand even in afflictions. He compared the Lord to a gardener who prunes plants so they bear more fruit. Pruning hurts, but it is not cruelty. It is the care of those who know what they are doing.
pt>en:7ae263fbc641cf56: Think of someone who is going through grief or a long trial. Write that person a short message, by hand or on their phone, with a verse from Isaiah 43 and the promise that you are praying. Sometimes, a simple letter is how God comforts.
pt>en:89e80f0df6592611: The theme running through the letters is the love of Christ. Rutherford said he had never known so much of the Savior's sweetness as he did in times of suffering. This does not mean he liked to suffer, but that he found in the trial a deeper communion with the Lord. The cross that weighed became for him a place of encounter.
pt>en:e23f387d44fb9cb0: Nine Marks of a Healthy Church (Nine Marks of a Healthy Church, 2000)
pt>en:ddca88563e1d7bd1: Samuel Rutherford was a 17th-century Scottish pastor, minister in a small rural parish, and later a theology professor. Because of his convictions, he was removed from the pulpit and sent away from his congregation. From that time of exile came many letters to friends, church members, and bereaved families. They are still read today as a treasure of consolation.
pt>en:d769e8dee6bfb924: Finally, he values biblical leadership, with qualified elders, and a culture of discipleship, in which more mature Christians help the younger ones grow. The health of the church does not depend on a famous leader, but on a people who build themselves up.
pt>en:22cbf553a20109b6: Another mark is membership taken seriously. Being a member is not having your name on a list, but making a commitment of love to concrete brothers. Duty also speaks of discipline in the church, which, when done with humility and patience, is an act of care that protects and restores.
pt>en:0c306b13e5ee052a: Duty insists that the church needs clarity about the gospel: God is holy, we are sinners, Christ died and rose again, and we are called to repentance and faith. Without this clarity, the church risks confusing conversion with an emotional decision or a change in behavior.
pt>en:7a4401a5d1fc48a8: Read Acts 2:42-47 this week and ask: what of this description already exists in my church and where can I help? Choose a person from the congregation to talk to, pray, and read the Bible together this month.
pt>en:f7cd8c15a0e7078e: Mark Dever, a Baptist pastor in Washington, United States, was concerned with a question that seems simple: what makes a church healthy? At a time when success was measured by numbers, events, and programs, he turned to the Scriptures and proposed some marks that help evaluate the life of a congregation.
pt>en:4ab96671b7b80bb6: The first mark, and the most important, is expository preaching: the one in which the sermon shows what the biblical text says and applies it to life. For Deer, the church is born and grows by the Word of God. When the pulpit faithfully explains the Bible, the flock is fed and God speaks to His people.
pt>en:8076d3cc985946f7: The dream that needs to die
pt>en:7c78a0b80abcfd2f: The book ends with the confession of sins among brothers. Bonhoeffer sees in it a way to break the isolation of sin. A reformed reading reminds us that confession is neither a sacrament nor a condition for forgiveness, but recognizes that confessing and praying for one another, as James commands, brings healing and humility.
pt>en:0a9d2c0a57fe16aa: Bonhoeffer speaks of simple services that keep communion alive: holding your tongue, being humble, helping with small things, carrying others' burdens, and above all, listening. Many Christians always want to speak, teach, and correct. Listening attentively is a form of love.
pt>en:3dda7aa31363c8aa: Thank God today for three brothers in your church, naming them. Then, look for one of them this week just to listen: ask how he is and don't rush to talk.
pt>en:b905cecbeea40027: Bonhoeffer begins by reminding us that being able to be with other Christians is a privilege, not something guaranteed. Many brothers live imprisoned, isolated, or persecuted. Therefore, every service, every meal with the church, and every visit from a brother must be received with gratitude, as a gift from God.
pt>en:b0766a876208307b: One of the strongest ideas in the book is that God destroys our idealized dreams of community. We arrive at church expecting perfect people and soon become disappointed. Bonhoeffer says this disappointment is healthy. Christian communion is not an ideal we built, but a reality God created in Christ. We love real brothers, with their flaws, because Christ loved them.
pt>en:9460de27dfae45fa: Psalm 133 in the Bible of SOLA
pt>en:bf595149d38a7502: Baptist Confession of Faith of 1689, chapters 28 to 30
pt>en:cec5ea81902f8129: The baptism of those who believe
pt>en:4a3d15fe4efd7a7b: If you were baptized, remember today what your baptism says: you died and rose with Christ. Read Romans 6 and prepare your heart for the next Supper, with confession and gratitude.
pt>en:9af933754149dce5: None of the ordinances save by itself. They point to Christ and strengthen the faith of those who receive Him.
pt>en:3f62ebbc976e790b: Baptism and Supper in the Baptist Confession of 1689
pt>en:9c38004124666509: Dietrich Bonhoeffer was a German Lutheran pastor who opposed Nazism and was executed in the final days of World War II. Before that, he ran an underground seminary where future pastors lived together. From this experience was born a short book about communal life among Christians, which remains relevant for the church today.
pt>en:4d2426f6fdf01fb7: Search: Baptist Confession of Faith of 1689
pt>en:78a6e318d4e9dd75: Confession calls baptism and the Supper ordinances instituted by the Lord Jesus Himself. They were not invented by the church and should not be altered by it. They must be administered in the local church, by those who have been called to do so, until the end of the world.
pt>en:b8e43cddd08a618e: The Baptist Confession of Faith of 1689 was written by Baptist churches in England that wanted to show their unity with other Reformers. It closely follows the Westminster Confession in almost everything, but differs on one important point: who should be baptized. Knowing this view helps to understand Baptist brothers and to converse with respect.
pt>en:2e30a2dda44b9032: Regarding the Supper, the 1689 Confession is very close to Westminster. It rejects the idea that bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ, and also denies that the Supper is merely an empty memory. Those who participate in faith receive and feed on the crucified Christ, in a real but spiritual way. The Supper also expresses the communion of believers among themselves.
pt>en:1417b6bf8362041f: In the chapter on baptism, Confession teaches that it is a sign of the believer's union with Christ in his death and resurrection, of grafting into him, of forgiveness of sins, and of surrendering oneself to God to live in newness of life. Therefore, it states that the proper subjects of baptism are those who profess repentance and faith. And it understands that immersion is the appropriate form. Presbyterian and Reformed continental brothers also baptize the children of believers, based on the covenant. It is a real difference, seriously debated, between people who confess the same gospel.
pt>en:23bb630d193882fe: Given for You: Reclaiming Calvin's Doctrine of the Lord's Supper (2002)
pt>en:16591b79e4e32b04: The Spirit unites heaven and earth
pt>en:410e5ca73846e121: Mathison also challenges churches to value the Supper in worship, celebrating it with reverence and joy. Calvin, he recalls, desired frequent celebration.
pt>en:ea48e3bc5951589f: The author reminds us that the Supper is not a reward for perfect Christians, but food for the weak. It strengthens faith, confirms promises, and deepens communion with Christ and the church. Those who examine themselves do not seek to discover if they are worthy on their own, but are trusting in Christ and reconciling with their brothers and sisters.
pt>en:1dfdd50bee9a5133: Before the next Supper at your church, read 1 Corinthians 11:23-29. Confess your sins, try to resolve some grief with a brother, and go to the table expecting to be nourished by Christ, not because of your strength, but because of His grace.
pt>en:ae2337349b982dd3: Keith Mathison, a theology professor linked to the Ligonier ministry, wrote a book to remind Reformed churches of a treasure many had forgotten: John Calvin's view of the Last Supper. He realized that many evangelicals treat the Supper merely as a moment of remembrance, and that this impoverishes church life.
pt>en:d231f3dc88f730d4: How is this possible if Christ ascended to heaven? Mathison explains Calvin's answer: the Holy Spirit is the bond that unites us to Christ. We do not pull Christ down; the Spirit lifts our hearts to Him. That is why the ancient liturgy told the people: lift up your hearts. At the Supper, faith receives the living Christ.
pt>en:86f0ebba15a9b180: The Great Commission is still valid
pt>en:c3abb1a0f5515ad8: Mathison shows that Calvin rejected two extremes. On one side, the idea that bread and wine physically become the body and blood of Christ. On the other, the idea that the Supper is just a symbol to recall something distant. For Calvin, and for Reformed confessions, at the Supper Christ truly nourishes us, not physically, but by the power of the Holy Spirit.
pt>en:88aee1e3f26445ce: An Enquiry into the Obligations of Christians to Use Means for the Conversion of the Heathens (1792)
pt>en:2058bac10e01f43f: Read Matthew 28:18-20 and ask how you can use the means God has given you. Choose a missionary or an unreached people to pray this week and, if possible, set aside an offering for your church's missionary work.
pt>en:ec9ce15b5573216e: In India, Carey faced years without conversions, illnesses, and painful family losses. Even so, he persevered. He worked with colleagues translating the Scriptures into several languages and left a planted church.
pt>en:d3a790eb8919172a: The gospel that arrived in Brazil
pt>en:9674a3128669e426: Many Christians at the time thought that Jesus' command to make disciples of all nations had been only for the apostles. Carey answered with a simple question: if Jesus' promise to be with us until the end of time still holds, why wouldn't the command hold? The mission belongs to the church of all generations.
pt>en:e8ac41f890a43e85: William Carey was an English shoemaker, poor and with almost no formal education, but passionate about the Bible and the world. While repairing shoes, he studied languages and maps. In 1792 he published a small book that helped ignite the modern missionary movement. The following year, he left for India, where he served until the end of his life.
pt>en:dcd22e42f831e16b: In a sermon that same year, Carey summed up his vision in a famous phrase: expect great things from God; try great things for God. Order matters. First we trust in the Lord's promises, then we act with courage.
pt>en:52cf71b4407c0cc2: The book's title speaks of using means. Carey firmly believes in God's sovereignty in salvation, but understood that God uses instruments. Just as merchants cross seas for profit, Christians should organize, pray, offer, and send people out of love for Christ. He proposed the creation of a missionary society, and the Baptists in his region founded it.
pt>en:194f39e374dd5d8b: Diary and ministry in Brazil (from 1859 onward)
pt>en:a69f4024010d5de0: Simonton faced harsh personal losses, including the death of his wife a few years after arriving. Still, he remained faithful until the end. His short life shows that God measures faithfulness, not just length of service.
pt>en:2cf1717365a8957c: Simonton dedicated his first months to learning Portuguese and getting to know Brazilian culture. He knew the gospel needed to be communicated in the language of the people. It began with small meetings, Bible classes, and personal conversations. The mission did not begin with grand events, but with patience and humility.
pt>en:21c3ed0728b4817a: Ashbel Green Simonton was a young Presbyterian pastor from the United States when he felt the call to serve in Brazil. He arrived in Rio de Janeiro in 1859, just over twenty-five years old. He died a few years later, still young, but planted the seed of the Presbyterian Church in the country. His story teaches a lot about mission.
pt>en:37bd2931ef590cb6: Read Romans 10:13-17 today and thank God for those who brought the gospel to Brazil. Then, think of someone close to you who does not yet know Christ and ask God for an opportunity to talk with them this week.
pt>en:ab4bcfe5b256cd0c: In a short time, the first Brazilians were baptized and a church was organized in Rio de Janeiro. Simonton understood that the mission does not end with conversion. It was necessary to form the church and prepare Brazilian pastors. He dedicated himself to teaching young people who would later continue the work.
pt>en:d6f51ac79d3eceff: The center of Simonton's work was the Bible. He preached, taught, and distributed the Scriptures, trusting that the Word of God would do its work. He also helped found an evangelical newspaper, the Evangelical Press, to take the message further. He believed that faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the Word of Christ.
pt>en:0e2f5fcc371679b2: The Inspiration and Authority of the Bible (The Inspiration and Authority of the Bible, 1948 collection)
pt>en:716dba2652ea0f97: Search: B. B. Warfield, Inspiration and Authority of the Bible
pt>en:2556b989f5c0c885: Paul says that Scripture is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and educating in righteousness. Warfield never separated doctrine from life. An inspired Bible is a Bible that must be read, believed, and obeyed.
pt>en:4f99a0edb53a5b0d: Warfield carefully studied the word Paul uses in 2 Timothy 3:16, translated as inspired. He showed that meaning is breathed by God. The idea is not that God breathed something special on a human text, but that Scripture came from the mouth of God. That is why it has the authority of God Himself.
pt>en:d65bc7d3c662c4a5: Warfield liked to remind us that trust in the Bible is not a church invention. It is the stance of Jesus himself and the apostles, who cited the Old Testament as the word of God and said that Scripture cannot fail. Following Christ includes receiving the Bible as he received it.
pt>en:f81f663c7dfc1836: At the same time, Warfield did not ignore human authors. Moses, David, Luke, and Paul wrote with their styles, vocabularies, and experiences. For him, God prepared these men throughout their lives and led them in such a way that they wrote exactly what He wanted. The Bible is entirely the word of God and the entire human word, without one thing nullifying the other.
pt>en:00462659d059b405: Read 2 Timothy 3 today. Before opening the Bible in the coming days, say a short prayer: Lord, speak, for your servant hears. Read expecting to hear the voice of God, not just information.
pt>en:405af51d1c8e1094: Benjamin Breckinridge Warfield was a professor at Princeton Seminary for more than thirty years, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. At a time when many scholars were beginning to treat the Bible as a merely human book, Warfield wrote with rigor and piety about the inspiration of the Scriptures. His essays on the subject were later collected in a volume that is still a reference.
pt>en:e1ca18e9285e3b02: How do we know that the Bible belongs to God?
pt>en:1820d1202e83bc29: The Inner Testimony of the Spirit
pt>en:4fa2d53930fdd22b: The church does not give authority to the Bible
pt>en:3c168e525dd813da: Institutes of the Christian Religion, Book I, chapters 6 to 9 (1559)
pt>en:2b6fb0f32a62e88c: Read Psalm 19 today and notice how David moves from the glory of heaven to the perfection of the Lord's law. Then, ask the Holy Spirit to open your eyes to see the wonders of the Word and to give you joy in obeying it.
pt>en:221c3346d4fb3220: Calvin also warned against those who claimed to have revelations of the Spirit apart from the Bible. The Spirit does not bring a new message; it seals and illuminates Scripture. Separating the two is losing both.
pt>en:60cf31325ced4220: One of the oldest questions about the Bible is this: how can we be sure that it is the Word of God? In the time of John Calvin, some said that the church is the one who gives authority to the Scriptures. In the early parts of the Institutes, Calvin answers differently and in a deeply comforting way.

pt>en:04b82bcee1bc0d4c: Why doesn't God simply forgive? Stott answers that forgiveness is not simple for a holy God. Sin is real, guilt is real, and God's justice cannot be ignored. At the same time, God is love and desires to save. On the cross, God's holiness and love meet.

pt>en:e26e6544cffa403a: Augustus Nicodemus Lopes, a Presbyterian pastor and Brazilian teacher, has dedicated many sermons and texts to the Holy Spirit. pt>en:305b7ba9252b1578: For Augustus, the clearest mark of the presence of the Spirit is the fruit described in Galatians 5: love, joy, peace, patience, goodness, faithfulness, meekness, and self-control. pt>en:a25279a12b114755: Augustus argues, with the Reformed tradition, that the Spirit acts through Scripture. He was the one who inspired the Bible, and it is he who illuminates it for us. pt>en:550fb8effbf74af1: Hoekema shows that this vision brings balance. We already have the Spirit, forgiveness, and new life, but we do not yet see complete victory. pt>en:fd216c5584fb50fe: One of the best-known chapters of the book deals with the new earth. Hoekema reminds us that Christian hope is not to float eternally in the clouds. pt>en:eb37fe76a43e8779: Anthony Hoekema was a professor of theology in Michigan, United States, and wrote one of the most balanced Reformed studies on the last things. pt>en:22f8d523db6d145b: Read Revelation 21:1-5 today and imagine, with the help of the text, the house God is preparing. Then, make a list of two things you can do this week as a sign of that hope: an act of justice, mercy, or reconciliation.

pt>en:a2c85ac940e0d0b1: Baxter himself lived with pain and illness for much of his life. He did not deny the suffering, but put it into perspective. The struggles of today are short compared to eternal rest. This hope helps the believer endure losses without despair.

pt>en:fecd08c3b6b871af: Therefore, following the holy fathers, all of us, by common agreement, teach men to confess one and the same Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, at once perfect in divinity and perfect in humanity, truly God and truly man, also consisting of rational soul and body; consubstantial to the Father according to divinity and, at the same time, consubstantial to us according to humanity; in all things similar to us, except in sin; begotten of the Father before the ages according to divinity, and, in these last days, for us men, and for our salvation, born of the virgin Mary, the mother of God (Theotókos), according to humanity; one and the same Christ, Son, Lord, Only Begot, recognized in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation; the distinction of natures is in no way annulled because of the union, but rather the properties of each nature are preserved, conspiring to form one person and one subsistence; not divided or separated into two persons, but one and the same Son, Only Begotten God, Word God, the Lord Jesus Christ; as from the beginning the prophets spoke about him, and the Lord Jesus Christ Himself taught us, and transmitted the creed of the fathers to us.
