pt>en:8917eb5f779024fb: Moreover, it is necessary for eternal salvation to also faithfully believe in the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ. For true faith is that we believe and confess that our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, is God and man. God, of the substance of the Father, begotten before the ages; and man, of the substance of his mother, born in time. Perfect God and perfect man, subsisting from a rational soul and human flesh. Equal to the Father according to divinity, and lesser than the Father according to humanity. Who, although God and man, is not two, but one Christ. One only, not by the conversion of divinity into flesh, but by the assumption of humanity into God. Entirely one, not by confusion of substance, but by unity of person. For just as the rational soul and the flesh are one man, so God and man are one Christ. Who suffered for our salvation, went down into hell, on the third day rose from the dead. He ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty, from where he will come to judge the living and the dead. At his coming, all men will rise with their bodies and give an account of their own works. And those who have done good will go to eternal life; and those who have done evil to eternal fire. This is the Catholic faith; whoever does not believe it true and firmly cannot be saved.
pt>en:25c368173524acb4: Everyone who wishes to be saved must, above all, profess the Catholic (universal) faith. Whoever does not keep it whole and inviolate will undoubtedly perish eternally. And the Catholic faith is this: that we worship one God in Trinity, and the Trinity in Unity; without confusing the Persons nor dividing the substance. For one is the Person of the Father, another that of the Son, and another that of the Holy Spirit. But the divinity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are one; equal to glory, coeternal majesty. As the Father is, so is the Son, and so is the Holy Spirit. The Father is uncreated, the Son is uncreated, and the Holy Spirit is uncreated. The Father is unlimited, the Son is unlimited, and the Holy Spirit is unlimited. The Father is eternal, the Son is eternal, and the Holy Spirit is eternal. And yet, there are not three eternals, but one eternal. Just as there are not three uncreated nor three unlimited, but one uncreated and one unlimited. Likewise, the Father is almighty, the Son is almighty, and the Holy Spirit is almighty. And yet, there are not three almighties, but one almighty. Thus, the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God. And yet, they are not three gods, but one God. Likewise, the Father is Lord, the Son is Lord, and the Holy Spirit is Lord. And yet, they are not three masters, but one Lord. Because, just as Christian truth obliges us to confess each Person, by themselves, as God and Lord, so too the Catholic religion forbids us to say that there are three gods or three masters. The Father was made by no one, neither created nor begotten. The Son is only of the Father; not made, nor created, but begotten. The Holy Spirit is of the Father and the Son; not made, nor created, nor begotten, but proceeding. There is, therefore, one Father, not three fathers; one Son, not three sons; one Holy Spirit, not three holy spirits. And in this Trinity none is before or after the other; none is greater or lesser than the other; but the three Persons are coeternal and equal among themselves. So that in everything, as has been said, the Unity in the Trinity and the Trinity in the Unity must be worshiped. Therefore, whoever wishes to be saved should think so about the Trinity.

pt>en:d8fb6f0ea2bbdca9: Abraham: the call to the unknown
pt>en:5704a36c319ace71: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph were not marble heroes. They lied, hesitated, fought within their families. Their story is, at its core, the story of God's patience with people like us.
pt>en:1243f78a4c205d93: SOLA Devotional Plans | Bible & Theology, organized into chapters. Each plan has the months in which it is offered ("months"). The themes are renewed each month; those who have already started a plan continue with it until it ends.
pt>en:a1ecec10c06ad651: God called Abram without handing over the map. He said "go," but didn't say where. Most of us want the complete roadmap before the first step. Faith, however, almost always works like car headlights on a road at night: it lights up just a few meters, enough to keep walking. Abram left at seventy-five years old. It's never too late to start obeying.
pt>en:5540ceed7e7f6c3a: What step is God asking you to take without seeing the whole path?
pt>en:1f552db2e211af2c: Which "familiar land" do you have difficulty leaving behind?
pt>en:65d90405a4ac67d5: Write in one sentence the next step of obedience you know you need to take, even without seeing the rest.
pt>en:0408306cc8d74ab8: What might God be asking you to put on the altar?
pt>en:815ce43c0bfc6a21: Isaac's question cuts the heart: "Where is the lamb?" Abraham answers with a phrase he himself did not fully understand: "God will provide." There are moments when faith has no explanation, only trust. And the definitive answer came centuries later, on another mountain, when God Himself gave the Lamb.
pt>en:843fe19f8913f3ce: Can you say "God will provide" before seeing the provision?
pt>en:7f6623119c44366b: Give today, in prayer, what you most fear losing, and say out loud: "God will provide."
pt>en:12418ae34ed78f4e: Isaac: the son of the promise
pt>en:92dd9b656441068b: Isaac was not a pioneer like his father. He reopened the wells that Abraham had dug. It may not seem heroic, but there is courage in caring for what we receive. When the neighbors fought over water, he did not fight; he dug another well. Sometimes victory is not in winning the argument, but in moving forward until we find space.
pt>en:b4c46b431988a2af: In which conflict do you need to stop fighting and digging elsewhere?
pt>en:25c64094d939d38d: What "wells" of faith inherited from other generations need to be reopened in your life?
pt>en:18d11f94b61ac7e6: Thank God today for a person who dug wells of faith before you, and, if you can, tell them so.
pt>en:b699ac8290d0eb74: Isaac went out to the field at dusk to meditate. The Bible keeps this simple scene: a man alone, thinking before God. It was there, at that unhurried moment, that he looked up and saw the answer to a prayer arrive. We live so busy that there is hardly any dusk left. And maybe we are missing exactly what God is bringing along the way.
pt>en:4243c39e5f2fc020: When was the last time you stopped without hurry before God?
pt>en:a482ac7dbe554cf5: What could be coming along the road while you're too distracted to see?
pt>en:3e6ab59c18610a3b: Set aside ten minutes today, without a cell phone, to walk or sit silently before God.
pt>en:e3ac6beec29a643c: In what difficult place can God be present without you realizing it?
pt>en:29073410f038402b: What does it change to know that God met Jacob in the middle of the flight?
pt>en:8670a19553e25d7c: Jacob ran away from home after deceiving his father and brother. He slept with a pillow stone and woke up saying, "The Lord is in this place, and I did not know." God does not expect us to be in good condition to appear. He visits fugitives. The loneliest place of your life may be the gate of heaven.
pt>en:2ef6ec848e9a51ec: Look at the hardest place of your week and write: "God is here."
pt>en:31915ba0639d7f56: Jacob spent his life fighting against everyone: his brother, his father-in-law, circumstances. That night, he fought with God. He left limping and with a new name. God sometimes defeats us to bless us. Jacob's limp was the mark that he no longer walked by his own strength alone.
pt>en:ee90219cc5e8f157: Against what, or against whom, have you been fighting with your own strength?
pt>en:2e55b97ce45d54d6: What "lameness" in your story could be a mark of an encounter with God?
pt>en:c32826534d6eecb4: Joseph: from the well to the palace
pt>en:8bfc9a821ad57dd6: Tell God sincerely where you are struggling, and ask for a blessing, not just a victory.
pt>en:8112b43aa5bb13ad: Joseph was sold by his brothers and became a slave in a strange land. And yet, the text repeats: "The Lord was with Joseph." It does not say that his life became easy. It says he was not alone. God's presence does not take us out of all wells, but transforms what happens inside them.
pt>en:a829918279b99152: Have you measured God's presence by the comfort of circumstances?
pt>en:f291d875a8b692d2: How can you be faithful in the "Egypt" you are in now?
pt>en:93bfc61a1f938fac: Do your work today with excellence, like Joseph, remembering that God is with you there.
pt>en:56a90609016352fe: After years, Joseph had the power to take revenge. He chose to forgive and said one of the Bible's deepest phrases: "You planned evil; God has turned it into good." He did not call evil good. He only recognized that God is greater than evil. That is theology learned through suffering, not in the classroom.
pt>en:a3b4365977cce249: What evil in your story have you still not delivered for God to transform?
pt>en:b7169ebe5089fb4c: Is there someone you need to free with your forgiveness?
pt>en:bb27c32081524e31: Pray for the name of someone who hurt you, asking God to turn that pain into good.
pt>en:aa26b9935ee227ef: Hebrews 11 is a gallery of imperfect people who trusted in a perfect God. None of them saw everything fulfilled. All saw enough to continue.
pt>en:2daf4f2ea58edbbc: Is your faith supported by God's character or favorable circumstances?
pt>en:3795f48214b0b808: Faith is not positive thinking nor religious optimism. It is trust supported by God's character. No one sees the wind, but everyone sees the trees moving. Faith is like this: it does not see God directly, but recognizes the marks of His action and decides to rely on Him.
pt>en:2f4904e9abd43c91: Note three pieces of evidence of God's faithfulness in your recent history.
pt>en:94cf94213af75578: Which "moving trees" show God's action in your life?
pt>en:16d42586ea0de2fb: Do you approach God out of trust or obligation?
pt>en:ebcc964bddf0d6e5: The verse is strong: without faith it is impossible to please God. Not because God requires a minimum level of enthusiasm, but because faith is essentially trusting that He is who He says He is. A child who does not trust the father may obey out of fear, but will have no intimacy. God wants children who come closer.
pt>en:3750266775d1250a: What does it mean, in practice, to seek God this week?
pt>en:1d412cd741ef7f34: Begin your prayer today by telling God who He is for you before asking for anything.
pt>en:b0c18c3946f4bfd2: What message would your life be preaching if it ended today?
pt>en:152c136f57ddea16: Abel died young and left no recorded word. Even so, the text says he still speaks. A life of faith continues preaching after it ends. We are all leaving some kind of echo. The question is: what will your life say when you are no longer here to explain?
pt>en:a575d4313792b3a1: Who spoke to your heart by faith, even after you departed?
pt>en:e92a80828fb0aed6: Write a sentence about the legacy of faith you want to leave.
pt>en:12c791c83a71c20c: Noah built a giant boat where it had never rained like that before. Imagine the neighbors' comments. Faith sometimes seems ridiculous to those who look from the outside. Noah did not have public approval, he had the word of God. And that was enough to hammer for many years.
pt>en:a5aea34ce7d23b67: What obedience of yours seems strange to others?
pt>en:5869c8b0453d93fe: Have you let other people's opinions define what you will do for God?
pt>en:ee077ab04cd57ddd: Take today a step of obedience that you have been avoiding out of fear of what others might think.
pt>en:0a98766b10da0e1a: What "treasure of Egypt" does your heart contend with with Christ?
pt>en:2f0ba934d76f9119: Identify a concrete choice this week in which you will place Christ above comfort.
pt>en:814e4e8f1a000649: What difficult choice are you putting off?
pt>en:768b5584c0e8300d: Moses had the palace, education, and future guaranteed. He chose to suffer with God's people. Faith is not just about believing; it is choosing. Every choice has a price, and so does every refusal. Moses looked beyond what he saw and considered that Christ was worth more than all the treasures of Egypt.
pt>en:e40525153fc3bc48: Have you ever considered yourself too unlikely for God to use?
pt>en:61fcbdd6dec7798c: Pray today for someone you think is too far from God.
pt>en:0e9fb51f3b46d62d: Who have you dismissed as "unlikely" and whom God can reach?
pt>en:a05e6e85d4f8ad5b: Among patriarchs and prophets appears Rahab, a foreign woman with a complicated past. She is in the gallery of faith and in Jesus' genealogy. God does not have a list of ideal candidates. He has a grace that reaches the unlikely. If Rahab is there, no one is too far away.
pt>en:f2174a349d0eb801: What weakness could your God use if you gave it to Him?
pt>en:75f69e76b86b9c0b: Have you been waiting to get strong before serving?
pt>en:66d76f679b18d353: Tell God, honestly, the weakness that shames you most, and ask for His strength.
pt>en:70b4212980962faa: Gideon was fearful, Samson was impulsive, David fell badly. Still, they are on the list. The text says that strength was drawn from weakness. The heroes of faith were not strong who became stronger; they were weak who leaned on God. This is good news for all of us.
pt>en:b8ed985bb3d38f1c: After the gallery, the author puts us on the track. The cloud of witnesses is not there to judge us, but to encourage us. And the center of it all is not any hero, it is Jesus, the author and finisher of faith. Runners who look back stumble. Runners who look toward the arrival continue.
pt>en:1ee68415d5d78ed8: What weight do you need to lose to run better?
pt>en:47cfdc7b8fe059d6: Where have your eyes been fixed lately?
pt>en:887f7db0b873f806: Choose a concrete weight (a habit, a resentment) and surrender it to God today.
pt>en:43fefe32041dbc6d: Fishermen, a tax collector, a skeptic, and a persecutor. Jesus did not choose the most prepared; He prepared those He chose.
pt>en:9704268295d6aff7: When was the last time Jesus' greatness brought him to his knees?
pt>en:3783bbbb0874b1c3: Which "boat" do you need to leave to follow it closer?
pt>en:8bd76a6d55333d67: After the miraculous catch, Peter does not celebrate. He falls to his knees: "Depart from me, I am a sinner." The holiness of Jesus exposed his smallness. But Jesus does not turn away; He calls. The first step of discipleship is to realize who we are before who He is.
pt>en:df4c52c230837258: Start the day by acknowledging before God an area where you need His grace.
pt>en:7cf3e7b8d5562b95: What "collection table" traps you to the past?
pt>en:0cb6fe6bbe6f246e: Matthew was a tax collector, someone the people hated. Jesus passed by the tax office and said two words: "Follow me." Matthew left the money table. How many people have we already discarded whom Jesus would call by name? And how many times do we think our past disqualifies us?
pt>en:b9ffc3f8775bad4c: Who have you considered unworthy of an invitation from Jesus?
pt>en:1d95d032b82b7a76: Invite someone unlikely today for coffee or a conversation about faith.
pt>en:4c6ea369d5d332f7: Can something good come from Nazareth?
pt>en:c57ffaceb504edfd: What prejudice could be preventing you from seeing something God is doing?
pt>en:a44d7b474c7fc792: Nathanael was prejudiced and did not hide it. Philip did not argue; he only said: "Come and see." Sometimes, the best argument is not a thesis, it is an invitation. Jesus was not offended by Nathanael's doubt; He revealed himself to him. Honest sincerity is usually closer to faith than polite indifference.
pt>en:4aee442dd73f51ec: Have you invited people to "come and see" or just tried to win arguments?
pt>en:7f7c82471af4bf54: Instead of arguing, tell someone today, simply, what Jesus did in your life.
pt>en:f335db2d9563fe76: Thomas was reputed to be unbelieving, but it was his one of the highest confessions in the New Testament. Jesus did not rebuke him harshly; he showed his wounded hands. Doubts, when brought to Jesus, can end in worship. The problem is not asking; it is running away with questions.
pt>en:5c2b5dfb0a4c3a0f: Write down your greatest doubt of faith and bring it to God in prayer, without fear.
pt>en:a5aa31fdce50f9f8: What doubt have you kept away from Jesus?
pt>en:85f25b16f2ebe182: What do Christ's wounds say about his questions?
pt>en:077cb48b6840eab9: What failure do you think disqualified you from serving God?
pt>en:2d01f0ee88c4cea6: Peter denied Jesus three times near a campfire. Jesus restores him with three questions near another campfire. He does not humiliate; he heals. And, with each answer, he returns to Peter a mission. Failure is not the end of the story of those who love Jesus; it can be the beginning of a humbler ministry.
pt>en:30e3882e6f059df6: If Jesus asked you today, "Do you love me?", what would you answer sincerely?
pt>en:6821256e087b0f5b: Answer Jesus' question in writing and think of a "sheep" you can care for this week.
pt>en:6ee0132ed606f101: Set aside time today just to be with Jesus, reading a Gospel without hurry.
pt>en:d87aaba09b9aaa35: The authorities saw two uneducated men speaking boldly and concluded: "They were with Jesus." It wasn't the diploma that impressed, it was the mark of coexistence. No one spends time with Jesus without it appearing. The question is whether people notice this in us.
pt>en:2b3d660f67b9718f: What do people perceive in you that can only come from living with Jesus?
pt>en:3dc0911127f84dd4: Have you spent time with him or just talked about him?
pt>en:e6992c597b79a209: Saul was going to Damascus full of certainties and left blind, guided by the hand. Sometimes God needs to take away our sight so that we can see. The church's greatest persecutor became its greatest missionary. No one is beyond the reach of grace, not even those who are fighting against it.
pt>en:c2df6fb40a26137c: Who did you stop praying for because you thought you would never change?
pt>en:ccc87f87bfbdf1b8: Return to praying today for the person you consider most distant from God.
pt>en:56c2bf36b046b15d: What certainty could your God be trying to tear down to show you something greater?
pt>en:15479d343884ac96: Paul writes about a prison, near the end. He does not talk about success, he talks about fidelity: I fought, I finished, I kept. It is a very different way of measuring life. In the end, the question will not be how much applause we receive, but whether we remain faithful until the finish line.
pt>en:c441f83b2436f760: How are you measuring the success of your life?
pt>en:34a1d5ddc9c9e5c3: What would it mean for you to "keep the faith" at this stage?
pt>en:3be4c69cfc3526f5: Write down what you wish you could say to God at the end of your journey.
pt>en:0b4e0dcabc242702: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel and Daniel
pt>en:f23575df86056194: Isaiah: the vision that changes everything
pt>en:53b1250bb572ca81: The prophets spoke in times of crisis, exile, and silence. They spoke of judgment, but always with stubborn hope. They are ancient voices for today's weary hearts.
pt>en:e89ad0a08a9a7b06: What "king" had to fall into your life for you to see the true King?
pt>en:71e932ff86684ba2: In the year the king died, Isaiah saw the King who never dies. The first reaction was not enthusiasm, it was heartbreak: "Woe is me." A true vision of God always gives us a true vision of ourselves. Anyone who has never felt small before God may not have truly seen Him yet.
pt>en:bf92dc0050dc1e35: Is your image of God big enough to break your pride?
pt>en:c73fdacb7539fc0a: Read Psalm 99 slowly and let God's holiness fill your prayer today.
pt>en:396dfa28eec93bbc: Have you conditioned your availability on knowing all the details?
pt>en:4cbbebec3ce92a19: Where might God be asking, "Whom shall I send?" in your life?
pt>en:1047bc01a72ca85c: After being purified, Isaiah hears the question: "To whom shall I send it?" He does not ask where or for how long. He only says: "Here I am." Availability comes before the task description. We usually ask for the contract before signing. Isaiah signed blankly.
pt>en:66f422a3de097a03: Pray today: "Here I am," and stay alert for a concrete opportunity to serve.
pt>en:bb287f35f432c34e: How does knowing that God knew you before you were born change the way you see yourself?
pt>en:0fafa7f11f306bcd: What excuse have you given God not to do what He asks?
pt>en:9bcf2134121b4ae6: Write your main insecurity and, next to it, the promise: "I am with you."
pt>en:d6abb811385e900b: Jeremiah thought he was too young. God replied that He knew him before the womb. Our insecurity usually looks inward: "I can't speak," "I'm not of age." God points outward: "I am with you." Vocation does not arise from our competence, but from the presence of the one who calls.
pt>en:a74f4fed7766ea43: The vase was ruined in the potter's hands, and he did not throw it away. He made another vase with the same clay. God does not give up the material just because the first shape did not work. Being clay is humiliating, but it is also hopeful: clay can still be shaped.
pt>en:f4199b233501de86: Are you resisting the Potter's hands or letting yourself be molded?
pt>en:1c8b0bada0309b2b: Give God in prayer an area of your life that you would like Him to redo.
pt>en:b53655250e66139e: What part of your life seems like a broken vase?
pt>en:34a3be1e63e5ad23: What do you usually remember on bad days?
pt>en:10aaa93700c10ecb: He does not afflict for pleasure
pt>en:d96e31d5ab0907bf: What truth about God do you need to remember today?
pt>en:37a3c356377bb7fa: Memorize Lamentations 3:22-23 and repeat whenever sorrow strikes.
pt>en:73a002d68ecdfd6e: Lamentations is a book of mourning about a destroyed city. And, right in the midst of pain, the prophet decides to bring something to memory. His hope does not arise from the landscape, but from the remembrance of God's character. There are days when faith is this: not feeling, but remembering.
pt>en:7795fa554bee9480: The text is delicate: God does not willingly afflict or sadden the children of men. Even discipline comes from a heart that does not take pleasure in our pain. This does not explain all suffering, but it changes the way we go through it. We are not in the hands of a cruel God, but of a Father who weeps with us.
pt>en:f0d68fffcf646ef7: What would it be like to bring their suffering to a Father who feels compassion?
pt>en:1f8694d4644838b1: Have you seen God as someone who rejoices in your pain?
pt>en:6399cbbd2e145c9f: Ezekiel: a life where there were only bones
pt>en:9d7dbb69a2611526: Write an honest prayer of lament, telling God what hurts, without pretending.
pt>en:74870fdd2a5b4788: Can you answer "You know" instead of "there's no way"?
pt>en:46a41e47882e2adc: Pray today specifically for the most "dead" situation you know, asking for the breath of the Spirit.
pt>en:7204002e4b315b8e: Which area of your life looks like a valley of dry bones?
pt>en:dea3feaf35ddc434: God takes Ezekiel to a valley of dry bones and asks: "Can these bones live?" The prophet's answer is wise: "You know it." He does not feign optimism nor give in to despair. He leaves the answer to God. And then the wind blows. No situation is too dead for the Spirit.

pt>en:1ad6c0da1dfbb93b: We want certainty before obeying, but spiritual life usually works the other way around: clarity comes as we walk. Calvin compared the Scriptures to glasses that correct our blurred vision. We don't see everything, but for the first time, we see the next step right.
pt>en:1dd51c0c194f2350: The clay lamp, with oil and wick, illuminated only a few steps ahead. The image recalls Israel in the desert, guided by a pillar of fire that showed the way night after night.
pt>en:6e69ea556bab2ee0: The Hebrew verb to trust (batach) brings the idea of supporting all your weight on something secure. To trust is to stop supporting oneself.
pt>en:ba761e93d94f1269: Abraham lived this when he left "not knowing where he was going." His story is that of someone who received promises greater than he could see.
pt>en:71ae2bd70ca04128: Jesus took trust to the extreme in Gethsemane: "Do not be as I want, but as you will." He trusted the Father even before the cross, and the Father vindicated him in the resurrection.
pt>en:1674d4e91986cac8: Trusting does not mean turning off the mind, but recognizing that it is not the last court. There are decisions where we have done everything possible and yet we need to deliver the result.
pt>en:e1666e77dc107345: God presents Himself with personal pronouns: "I am with you," "I am your God," "I strengthen you." And He speaks of His "right hand," a symbol of power that sets you free, as in Exodus.
pt>en:1d47bb7388315395: Isaiah 40 to 55 speaks to an exiled people in Babylon, far from the earth and with the feeling that God had forgotten them. It is in this scenario that the "Do not fear" sounds.
pt>en:2cd9c7e944074767: Fear usually speaks to the future: what if it goes wrong? God's promise speaks to the present: I am with you. It does not eliminate tomorrow, but returns us to today.
pt>en:5dfed25da3df8f4e: That is why Jesus' phrase is so strong: "I am the true vine." He is faithful Israel, the one who finally bears the fruit God always sought.
pt>en:904fcda913135630: The Greek verb menō, to remain, appears repeatedly in John 15. It speaks of dwelling, staying, making a dwelling, as one settling in a house and not just visiting it.
pt>en:d2601058b9c58fd2: We live trying to produce spiritual results by willpower. Jesus reminds us that fruit is the result of connection, not haste.
pt>en:5963870c14e8a60b: Paul uses temple language. In place of animals offered and killed, he speaks of a "living sacrifice": the whole life given to God as worship (latreia).
pt>en:a923b85bb8756b36: "Do not conform" can be understood as not letting oneself be shaped by the form of this world. Instead, "transform" (metamorphoō), the same root used for the transfiguration of Jesus.
pt>en:c30d6b1f2791dea3: Hebrews was written to weary and persecuted Christians, tempted to turn back. Chapter 11 is a gallery of people who kept walking without seeing the end of history.
pt>en:4e215d3d58a408ab: This change begins in the mind. Paul is not talking only about a change in behavior, but about a new way of thinking, learned from the Word and the Spirit.
pt>en:1ceec3892e48b2dc: Reformed thinkers like Herman Dooyeweerd insisted that no one thinks neutrally: every thought is born from a heart that worships something. That is why transformation begins in worship. We truly change when what we love changes.
pt>en:22b0cf1b5479852b: We are shaped every day by what we see, hear, and repeat. Mind renewal is a slow path of exchanging old lies for God's truths.
pt>en:39e1d28b2eba8d42: Faith is called the "certainty" of things that are expected. The word hypostasis brings the idea of something firm, which provides support, as a foundation on which one can stand.
pt>en:c51351800b4136b7: Hebrews 12 concludes by pointing to Jesus, "author and finisher of faith." Faith is not leap into the dark, it is looking at Him and running with perseverance.
pt>en:2518ec79096f778d: In a pending decision, pray asking for direction and talk to someone mature in faith before deciding.
pt>en:b16bdb9877b6bf62: Choose a verse to memorize this week and read it in the morning and at night.
pt>en:f6e0dc256f2c75ae: Trusting wholeheartedly is different from understanding everything. Proverbs calls us to recognize the Lord in all ways, including those where our understanding fails.
pt>en:d4da2444e1305410: The old lamp did not illuminate the entire road, only the next step. The Word of God guides us thus: with enough light to obey today, even when the whole path is not yet clear.
pt>en:869d8567538b8e1d: When fear appears today, repeat the verse quietly and turn fear into a specific prayer.
pt>en:e8ee0f66622ddb5f: The reason not to fear is not the strength of the people, but the presence of the Lord: "I am with you," "I am your God." Christian courage is a response to a promise, not an effort of self-confidence.
pt>en:915b44932fc4ea60: Set aside a fixed time of day for prayer and reading and treat this meeting as a non-negotiable commitment this week.
pt>en:172c044db0bc0e61: After setting out God's mercies, Paul calls for the giving of the whole life as worship. Transformation happens through the renewal of the mind, learning to think according to God's will and not according to the mold of this age.
pt>en:f6394f8e698c2ac8: Read the entire Hebrews 11 and choose a character to observe how their faith was shown in actions.
pt>en:f4fe661a6c30d640: Hebrews define faith as firmness regarding what is expected and conviction in what is not seen. Faith is not a leap into the dark: it rests on the word of God who created the world and fulfills what He promises.

pt>en:d07e857a0d649021: God whispers in our pleasures, speaks in our conscience, but cries out in our pains: they are His megaphone to awaken a deaf world.
pt>en:8084ed78cb6457f7: There is no well so deep that God's love is not even deeper.

pt>en:64abd92e19fca5f7: Give what you command, and command what you want.

pt>en:ac18bde108b4ae11: In prayer, it is better to have a heart without words than words without a heart.

pt>en:157db9f3242c24ec: Solved: live with all my strength as long as I live.
pt>en:e4221a1e0ca35484: The world is the theater of God's glory.
pt>en:06ba3e049360b6c2: Cheap grace is grace without discipleship, grace without the cross.
pt>en:dc83260e69c97205: What is your only comfort in life and in death? That I do not belong to myself, but to my faithful Savior Jesus Christ.
